header.name: Large Language Models
header.description: In recent years, Large Language Models (LLMs) have become integral to the field of Natural Language Processing (NLP), significantly enhancing the performance of essential NLP tools. This course offers a comprehensive introduction to language modeling and its diverse applications, providing a self-contained overview. Starting with the foundational probabilistic principles of language models, the course delves into the formal and theoretical aspects of what defines a language model. This all-encompassing program empowers participants with the essential knowledge and skills to effectively utilize LLMs. Covering theoretical principles and practical applications, the course provides a complete grasp of LLMs and their varied real-world applications. The course introduces recent literature in different areas related to LLMs in a seminar style. The students registering for this course should have basic knowledge in DL.

prerequisites.raw: NLP (CSE556), Deep Learning (ECE553) or Theories of Deep Learning (CSE516/ECE559) or Advances in Deep Learning (ECE677/CSE677)

cos.label: CO1
cos.text: Students will be able to comprehend the fundamental concepts and models in NLP, including an in-depth knowledge of LLMs and their applications

cos.label: CO2
cos.text: Students will be able understand the underlying architecture of transformers and apply their applications to not only in NLP but also in other domains like computer vision

cos.label: CO3
cos.text: Students will be able to develop approaches to find solutions for different real-world problems using LLMs

cos.label: CO4
cos.text: Students will be able to critically assess the capabilities and limitations of LLMs, as well as identify security risks associated with their use

lecture_weeks.topic_raw: Introduction, overview of the NLP models
Introduction and What are Large Language Models?
In-Context Learning, Prompting and Zero-shot Inference
Emergent Ablities and Scaling Laws for LLM
RLHF and Instruction Tuning, Multimodal LLMs

resources.title_raw: Recent papers on LLMs will be shared in the class.
Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing, 3rd ed
Manning and Schütze, Foundations of Stat NLP
Murphy, Machine Learning: a Probabilistic Perspective
On the Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models (published by Stanford researchers in July 2021) surveys a range of topics on foundational models (large langauge models are a large part of them).
A Primer in BERTology: What we know about how BERT works provides an excellent overview of what we understand about BERT (last update: Nov 2020).
